title: Physical Insights into the Leakage Mechanisms Governing the Scaling Trends in 4H-SiC Based Junctionless FETs
problem: Wide bandgap semiconductors like 4H-SiC enable advanced devices for high-voltage and high-temperature applications, but leakage mechanisms differ from silicon. Understanding sub-10nm 4H-SiC junctionless FET leakage is critical for design optimization.
motivation: Sub-10nm scaling of 4H-SiC junctionless FETs requires understanding which leakage mechanisms dominate (unlike silicon where band-to-band tunneling dominates). Design guidelines for advanced nodes need physical insight into leakage trade-offs.
method: 2D device simulation (calibrated) analyzing three main leakage components: (1) GIDL via gate-induced drain leakage (band-to-band tunneling), (2) direct gate tunneling, (3) inefficient volume depletion. Comparison of silicon vs. 4H-SiC physics.
key_novelty: First comprehensive analysis of leakage mechanisms in 4H-SiC ultra-short channel JLFETs revealing dominant mechanisms differ from silicon; direct gate tunneling and volume depletion control leakage in sub-10nm regime.
contributions: Comprehensive leakage mechanism analysis for 4H-SiC JLFETs
Identification of three main leakage components
Proof that L-BTBT GIDL not dominant in 4H-SiC (vs. silicon)
limitations: Simulation-based analysis only; no experimental validation; specific leakage values not provided in abstract; limited to 4H-SiC material; design guidelines provided but not quantitatively specified.
primary_theme: Device physics for wide bandgap scaling
